judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short sentence; the qualifier 'if any' is loose but the disclaimer is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.03(b), under which the Master Servicer may step in as servicer, and with Section 8.03's limitations on liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bond and policy need only be 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees' — a standard with no ascertainable content and no minimum amount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision fixes the coverage level, so the vagueness is not cured elsewhere; it sits alongside Section 8.03's liability limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants power to do 'any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable' followed by a non-exhaustive four-item list ('including but not limited to'), then a REMIC-protective proviso turning on what is 'reasonably within its control'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is subject to 'the provisions of Article XI' and Section 4.03, and its co-trustee limb points to Section 10.11; the discretion granted must be read against the Accepted Master Servicing Practices standard in Section 4.01.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Almost wholly circular — every obligation is qualified by 'in accordance with this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement', and the release limb is permissive ('may be released') without saying by whom or on what terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The substantive due-on-sale rules live in the Servicing Agreements, which are exhibits rather than operative text here, so this section supplies no independent standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but procedurally concrete; the parenthetical 'or if the related Servicer does not, the Master Servicer may' creates a permissive backstop whose trigger is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses Exhibit G, the Request for Release form (c282), and interacts with Section 4.12's requirement that the Custodian retain Mortgage Files; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The third sentence begins 'Such trust receipt shall obligate the related Servicer' although no trust receipt has been mentioned anywhere in the subsection — a dangling referent in the operative obligation to return the Mortgage File.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The document actually described is the Exhibit G request for release, and Section 4.12 requires the Custodian to retain each Mortgage File; the missing trust-receipt concept has to be supplied from the Custodial Agreements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains two broken constructions — 'The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access' (missing conjunction) and 'to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — which obscure who is entitled to access.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A near-identical access regime already appears in Section 4.01 with different beneficiaries (Certificateholders, the FDIC and its examiners) and a different cost rule, so the two overlap imperfectly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Repeats the same missing conjunction ('the Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall be entitled to setoff') and grants a setoff right for amounts 'properly due and payable' without further definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The setoff right qualifies the declaration that the funds 'shall be and remain the sole and exclusive property of the Trustee', and must be squared with the permitted withdrawals in Sections 5.01 and 5.03.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to 'insurers meeting the eligibility requirements set forth in this Agreement and the related Servicing Agreement' and to a no-additional-insurance rule expressed by double negative; workable but not self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This Agreement does not itself set out insurer eligibility requirements anywhere — the Insurance Policy and LPMI Policy definitions only reference Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac standards for LPMI — so the cross-reference is to a standard that is not there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Procedurally clear, with an express carve-out for restoration amounts and a rule that added costs are ignored for distribution purposes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites Sections 5.01 and 5.04 as the deposit authority and Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04 for withdrawals, but the table of contents titles Section 5.04 the 'Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex', which is not an account-withdrawal provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but bounded; 'such actions ... as shall be necessary to realize recovery' is a purposive standard with an illustrative list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Insurance Proceeds definition (c166) and Section 4.11(b) on presenting claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Uses the compound standard 'best reasonable efforts' and the awkward 'the Master Servicer, the related Servicer' construction again; the prohibitions themselves are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Primary Mortgage Insurance Policy definition (c239) and the LPMI Policy definition; the nested 'to the extent required under this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement' qualifiers make the obligation contingent on documents outside this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear as to the duty to present claims; the deposit mechanic is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs deposit 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05', but this Agreement has no Section 5.05 — Article V ends at Section 5.04 — so the authority cited does not exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent available' and 'until all amounts distributable ... have been distributed in full and the Master Servicer otherwise has fulfilled its obligations' are soft, but the custody duty is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.02, 4.07 and the Custodial Agreements; the retention duty dovetails with the release mechanics in Section 4.07.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As come into and continue in default and as to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection' is an open standard, and 'otherwise comparably convert' is a general catch-all after two specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Liquidated Loan, Final Recovery Determination and REO Property definitions and Section 4.15.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear in its components: the fee, float income, an expense-bearing rule and a Compensating Interest offset.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The float income is granted here, again in the Master Servicing Fee definition (c186) and again in Master Servicing Compensation (c185) — three provisions granting the same entitlement, which risks double counting in the Interest Funds calculation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As expeditiously as possible' is an open timing standard; the REMIC foreclosure-property conditions are precisely cited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.02's REMIC covenants and the REO Property and REO Imputed Interest definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Protected Account definition (c245) and Section 4.15(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso refers to 'any such unreimbursed Monthly Advances', a term this Agreement never defines and which does not match the 'Advances' referred to in the first half of the same sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Monthly Payment' and now 'Monthly Advances' are both undefined imports; the reimbursement priority also has to be read against the Liquidation Proceeds definition (c176), which already deducts unreimbursed Advances and Servicing Fees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net of any payment to the Master Servicer and the related Servicer as provided above' plus fixed deposit and remittance dates; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c396, the Determination Date (c135) and Remittance Date (c276) definitions, both of which vary by Servicer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but concrete, save that it 'deems' non-compliance an Event of Default and then declares 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary' — a sweeping override whose reach is not delimited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deemed Event of Default and the mandatory immediate termination sit against Section 9.01, which defines Events of Default and normally supplies cure periods, and against the Master Servicer's termination and successor provisions in Sections 8.05-8.06; the supersession clause is precisely the sort of override that has to be reconciled with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An intricate Regulation AB compliance regime with several nested 'to the extent' qualifiers, plus the same unbounded 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Like Section 4.16 it converts a reporting failure into an Event of Default with immediate termination, overriding Article IX; it also makes obligations depend on Exhibit N, which Section 4.17's own Servicing Criteria definition allows the parties to revise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long and procedurally dense with several mis-set enumerators ('(1)' for '(i)'), but the deadlines and allocations of responsibility are specific and the liability carve-out is carefully worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly relies on the representation in Section 2.04(vi) and on Exhibit O's allocation of reporting parties, and cross-refers to Sections 4.18(a)(iv), 4.18(a)(vi)(B), 6.06 and 12.05; those references hold together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Parallel to the Form 10-D regime and equally detailed; enumerators are again garbled and one deadline reads 'the 4 Business Day', but the scheme is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c400 and Exhibit O; the Reportable Event definition (c281) points back here.
